data.cultural_impact: The name Hadiyya is of Arabic origin and in Arabic culture, it is a name given to a precious gift, sometimes given as a bridal name or a name given to a child born on a significant day. It is a name that signifies generosity and kindness as it implies the giving and receiving of gifts. In some Muslim communities, Hadiyya is also a term used for the Sadaqa or Iftar gift given during the month of Ramadan, further emphasizing the theme of giving and generosity.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Hadiyya holds great significance for Muslims as it is often seen as a reminder of the blessings and generosity of Allah. In the Hadith, it is mentioned that the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) once said, “When Allah Almighty loves a person, He calls Jibrael (Gabriel) and says: 'O Jibrael! I love so and so, so love him.' The angel then inspires the hearts of the community to love that person and if he is alive, he is filled with peace and delight. When somebody is favoured by Allah in this manner, it is said that he is given the rank of Hadiyyatun Larbiyah or 'one who has been bestowed a priceless gift,'" (Bukhari and Muslim). This hadith emphasizes the spiritual significance of receiving a gift from Allah, and the great blessings and prosperity that come with it.
